_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 4.4. No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

questions.scenario: For the offence of sexual activity with a child (s. 9), what age must the offender be?
A, aged 20, has consensual sexual activity with B, aged 15. A reasonably believed B was 16. Which is correct?
options: Not guilty of s. 9 – reasonable belief that B was 16 or over
explanations: Belief is relevant when B is 13–15.

questions.scenario: A, aged 20, sexually touches B, aged 12, believing reasonably she is 16. Which offence?
options: Sexual assault of a child under 13 (s. 7) – belief is irrelevant

questions.scenario: A, aged 17, has sexual activity with B, aged 14. Which section applies?
options: s. 13 – child sex offences committed by a person under 18

questions.scenario: What is the maximum penalty for s. 13 (under-18 offenders)?
A, 30, has sex with his girlfriend in front of her 10-year-old son, knowing he is watching, for sexual gratification. Which offence?
options: Engaging in sexual activity in the presence of a child (s. 11)
explanations: s. 12 is about causing the child to watch – possible, but s. 11 fits presence.

questions.scenario: A shows a 13-year-old pornographic videos on his phone for his own sexual gratification. Which offence?
options: Causing a child to watch a sexual act (s. 12) – includes images

questions.scenario: For s. 15 (meeting a child following sexual grooming), how many previous occasions of meeting or communicating are required?
A, 35, has chatted online once with a 13-year-old and travels by train to meet her intending sexual activity. Police stop him at the station. Which is correct?
options: Full s. 15 offence – travelling with intent to meet is enough
No offence – no meeting took place

questions.scenario: The '14-year-old girl' A has been talking to is actually an adult police officer. A travels to meet her. Which is most appropriate (⚠)?
Under s. 15A, the communication must be for the purpose of…
What is the age limit for the victim in s. 15A sexual communication with a child?
Which communication is caught by s. 15A?
options: A communication that is sexual, or intended to encourage B to make a sexual communication
Only messages in a public forum

questions.scenario: A organises a hotel room so that his friend can have sex with a 14-year-old. Which offence?
options: Arranging or facilitating a child sex offence (s. 14)

questions.scenario: For abuse of a position of trust (s. 16), the victim must be…
A teacher, 28, has a sexual relationship with a 17-year-old pupil at his school. Which offence?
options: Abuse of a position of trust (s. 16)

questions.scenario: Since 2022, which positions were added to positions of trust (⚠)?
Which is a defence to abuse of a position of trust?
options: A and B were lawfully married or in a sexual relationship before the position of trust arose

questions.scenario: A step-father has sexual activity with his 17-year-old step-daughter. Which offence?
options: Sexual activity with a child family member (s. 25)

questions.scenario: Under the Protection of Children Act 1978, a 'child' means a person under…
A downloads indecent images of children onto his laptop. Following R v Bowden, this is…
What is the maximum penalty for possession of indecent photographs of a child (s. 160 CJA 1988)?
Which of these is a defence to possession under s. 160?
options: A thought the child looked over 18
A had not seen the image and didn't know, or have cause to suspect, it was indecent

questions.scenario: A man, 30, holds images of his 17-year-old wife. Which defence may apply?
options: Marriage/partnership defence where the child was 16 or 17

questions.scenario: A drawing or cartoon showing a child in sexual activity is…
options: A possible prohibited image of a child (Coroners and Justice Act 2009, s. 62)

questions.scenario: What is a 'pseudo-photograph'?
options: An image made by computer graphics or otherwise which appears to be a photograph

questions.scenario: A, 25, sends a 15-year-old a message asking her to send him a topless photo; she refuses. Which offence fits best?
options: Causing or inciting a child to engage in sexual activity (s. 10)

questions.scenario: How are indecent images of children graded for sentencing?
Who decides whether a photograph is 'indecent'?
options: The jury/magistrates applying recognised standards of propriety

questions.scenario: A, 40, chats online once with a 15-year-old and then arranges to meet her for sex next week. Which is correct?
options: s. 15 – arranging to meet is enough
